active_alert.headline: Large Group / Catering Ticket Spike (AOV $915.76 vs $28.50 Normal)
active_alert.immediate_present_status: Counter ticket size jumped to $915.76/order (+3113% above normal). Multiple high-density platters (King of the Hill $145, Bevo $79, Pitmaster $54) or bulk meat pounds are clearing the cutting block.
active_alert.causal_explanation: Large office/family group orders concentrated in the 08:00 window. While ticket volume (1 orders) is steady, meat poundage per transaction has doubled, pulling multiple briskets from holding.
active_alert.recommended_pit_action: Carve whole briskets to order rather than pre-slicing to preserve moisture; alert the prep cook to replenish bulk pint containers of potato salad and mac & cheese.

PAR Level.definition: The exact target quantity of cooked meat, prepped sides, or raw stock that must be on hand at each shift change to satisfy anticipated demand without running out or over-prepping.
PAR Level.how_it_helps: Prevents 86ing meat during peak lunch and stops costly end-of-day waste by establishing strict morning and afternoon slicing thresholds.

AOV.definition: The average dollar amount spent per customer transaction, calculated as Total Revenue divided by Total Order Count.
AOV.how_it_helps: Detects whether high volume is driven by hundreds of small individual sandwiches or a few high-dollar Texas feast platters ($145 King of the Hill), allowing the cutting board to pace whole-muscle slicing.

Z-Score.definition: A statistical measure indicating how many standard deviations current hourly sales or order velocity deviate from the historical average for that specific hour and day of week.
Z-Score.how_it_helps: Filters out normal small fluctuations: a Z-score above +1.5 immediately flags a statistically significant rush requiring urgent pitmaster intervention.

Meat Draw.definition: The velocity (in pounds per hour) at which finished meat is carved and removed from the 140°F holding cabinet to fulfill guest trays.
Meat Draw.how_it_helps: Alerts the pitmaster hours in advance if current carve velocity will cause an early sellout before dinner, giving time to throttle portion sizes or push combo sausages.

Cooked Yield %.definition: The percentage of usable, saleable meat remaining after trimming and smoking, calculated as (Finished Sliced Weight / Raw Untrimmed Weight) * 100.
Cooked Yield %.how_it_helps: Ensures true wholesale meat costs are accounted for. Choice packer brisket yields ~50-52%, meaning a $5.08/lb raw brisket actually costs ~$10.00/lb on the cutting board.

Shrinkage.definition: The loss of raw meat weight during smoking caused by moisture evaporation and fat rendering (typically 48-50% for brisket, 40-42% for pork butt).
Shrinkage.how_it_helps: Calibrates pitmaster smoker humidity and wrapping timing; excessive shrinkage means dry meat and lost profit per rack or packer.

COGS.definition: The direct expenditure for raw meat, spices, peach paper, sauce, and takeout containers required to produce a menu item.
COGS.how_it_helps: Reveals the exact cost per serving so menu prices ensure sustainable margins even when raw beef prices fluctuate.

Food Cost %.definition: Portion Cost of Goods Sold divided by the Retail Selling Price, expressed as a percentage.
Food Cost %.how_it_helps: Industry target for Texas BBQ is 28-32%. Identifying items above 40% (like unbundled brisket sandwiches) guides pricing corrections and portion controls.

Gross Margin %.definition: The percentage of revenue remaining after subtracting COGS: (Retail Price - COGS) / Retail Price * 100.
Gross Margin %.how_it_helps: Provides the cash necessary to pay pitmasters, seasoned post oak wood deliveries, kitchen rent, and smoker equipment upkeep.
